specialist_findings.claim: The plan asserts the estate has grown ~33% to ~550 non-archive docs (line 31), but this is an admitted estimate ('an estimate; Pass 0 measures the actual count', line 136). The scale assumption drives the concurrency-cap, loop-until-dry iteration budget, and session sizing for the dedicated run. If the actual count is substantially different the orchestration shape may be miscalibrated before promotion.

The plan states the strategic-choice registry ('the 12 bets') is 'already signed off' (line 171) and marks it as blocking for the plans-to-choices traceability pass. This is an unverified inherited claim; the plan does not cite the registry artefact path or a commit/SHA. If the registry has since changed in scope or has open ratification items, the traceability pass can produce false-orphan classifications.

The promotion trigger (line 204-209) requires the plan node-schema lens and the strategic-choice registry, then defers finalising 'finding schemas, specialist routing table, workflow scripts, and report directory' to promotion time. This defers a significant proportion of the operationalisation assumptions to a future moment. If those artefacts require owner-level decisions (e.g. schema shape, concurrency cap), the promotion handoff may block on more than is signalled.

The floor of three reads per document (line 78-79) is stated as the minimum, but the specialist routing logic (lines 88-93) routes by content signal and tops up with conformance reader and assumptions-expert only when fewer than two specialists are routed. There is no explicit statement of what happens when a document genuinely produces zero specialist content signals — the floor could collapse to holistic + conformance reader (two, not three) before the top-up logic fires.

The plan assumes dynamic multi-agent orchestration via the Workflow tool or platform equivalent (line 125-126) is available at promotion time. The parenthetical 'on Claude Code the Workflow tool, or the platform's equivalent multi-agent primitive' acknowledges uncertainty but does not require a pre-promotion availability check. If the Workflow tool is unavailable, the wall-clock advantage of pipelined fan-out collapses to a sequential single-agent run, which materially changes the survey timeline.

The loop-until-dry exit criterion (two consecutive critic rounds surface nothing new, line 121) is sound in principle but assumes the completeness critic itself has full coverage of what was dropped. If the critic's own scope is bounded by the same truncation risks flagged in the Risks table (line 199), the dry signal may be false. The plan does not require the critic to be a fresh agent blind to the prior round.

specialist_findings.claim: The plan explicitly builds on graph-core and graph-project as the substrate (Pillar 2) and references ADR-179 as the transport-agnostic authority. The architectural dependency is declared as 'beneficial, not blocking' for Stage 1, which is appropriate given graph-core already exists. No parallel graph stack is introduced.

The schema-first pillar (Pillar 1) consciously extends the repo's Cardinal Rule — upstream OpenAPI spec as single schema source — into a second domain (document-type schemas). The plan is explicit that it applies the principle by analogy, not by extending or restating the Cardinal Rule itself. This is a clean architectural boundary.

Stage 3 pulls the 'thread' node-type forward from a later stage because the restructure cannot site plans in threads without it. This is architecturally sound reasoning but creates an implicit multi-type build within Stage 3 (plan + thread node-schemas). The plan acknowledges this promotion but the Stage 3 acceptance criteria (lines 519-522) does not explicitly reference thread-node conformance as a deliverable. If thread-schema is under-specified at Stage 1 promotion, Stage 3 may encounter a blocking gap.

The evidence-ingestion actuation layer (Stage 4) names five external sources — Vercel, Sentry, Sonar, GitHub, PostHog — but explicitly defers all connector technology, orchestration, and write-back validation decisions to promotion time. For an architecture where 'the actuation layer is the load-bearing, still-to-be-designed work', deferring technology selection risks the rest of the graph contract being shaped by assumptions that the later connector choices may not support. The risk table names this indirectly but does not flag connector-technology pre-constraints as a design risk.

The authority model (Pillar 3) specifies that 'no continuity record is citable as scope authority' as a graph invariant. This is a strong machine-checked assertion. However, the plan does not describe where or how this invariant is enforced — whether by the observe-mode extractor (Stage 1.4), a separate validator, or a later warn/enforce escalation stage. Without an enforcement home, the invariant is a principle, not a structural property.

The plan commits the node-type set, edge vocabulary, authority model, and external-edge vocabulary as a v1 contract to be ratified before any build, but explicitly states the concrete taxonomy is 'survey-gated' (Stage 2). This creates a sequencing ambiguity: Stage 1.1 ratifies the shape, Stage 2 refines the taxonomy, but Stage 1.3 (the strategic-choice registry) and Stage 1.4 (the extractor) must implement parts of the schema before the survey refines it. If Stage 2 causes additive changes to edge types used in Stage 1.3/1.4, those deliverables need rework. The plan calls Stage 2 refinement 'additive' but does not formally constrain what counts as additive vs. breaking for already-built Stage 1 components.

The DORA attribution mechanism depends on every change tracing to a plan serving a strategic choice to be classified as 'planned' versus 'rework'. This requires complete and correct serves_strategic_choice wiring across all plans. The plan acknowledges the estate currently has unvalidated frontmatter and convention-only relationships. Until Stage 3 completes the restructure, the rework-attribution traversal will produce unreliable results — a structural gap between the architectural design intent and what the graph can actually compute from the real estate, for an extended period spanning Stages 1-3.

The plan explicitly reserves validated_by and cost/accuracy evidence edges in node-schema #1's vocabulary and cross-references plan-node-schema.v0.md section 5.5. This is sound forward-design: the edge vocabulary is reserved in the contract before the actuation layer is built, avoiding retrofit. The boundary between 'reserved in v0' and 'built in Stage 4' is explicit.

The no-PII constraint (Pillar 6, Boundaries) is architecturally concrete: external identifiers live only in gitignored local config. This is a structural boundary, not a policy statement, and it is consistent across the plan. No architecture smell here.

specialist_findings.claim: The plan's dependency direction 'agent-tools -> agent-graphs/practice-graph -> graph substrate' (lines 418-422) is stated as an existing ADR-179 decision, but it is sourced from a sibling future-status plan ('agent-graphs-workspace-organisation.plan.md') not from ADR-179 itself. ADR-179 only records that CLI surfacing belongs in agent-tools. Treating a future-lifecycle suggestion plan as a ratified architectural direction risks building on an unratified dependency model.

Open question 4 (line 550) asks how much of existing graph-core vocabulary to reuse, yet the plan simultaneously instructs 'Do not create a parallel graph/tooling stack' (line 425) and lists non-goal 'Do not create graph substrate code that depends on agent-tools' (line 532). These constraints together leave the integration path architecturally unresolved: the plan cannot rule out a parallel stack while also deferring the answer to whether to reuse graph-core. This is a structural contradiction in the proposed architecture, not merely an open question.

The relationship schema YAML examples (lines 319-355) include a 'value_stream' and 'strategic_choice' as valid edge targets (e.g. supports.to includes 'value_stream', 'strategic_choice'), but neither 'value_stream' nor 'strategic_choice' appears in the document type model table (lines 213-228). If these are real node types they must be in the type registry; if they are properties of strategy documents, the edge targets are mistyped. Either way the schema examples are internally inconsistent with the type model.

The plan defers the schema language decision to open question 2 (line 543: JSON Schema, Zod, TypeScript types, or generated combination) while also specifying a 7-phase delivery timeline and Phase 2 schema definitions. Choosing the schema authority mechanism is load-bearing for validator implementation (Phases 3-5) and for graph-core vocabulary reuse (open question 4). Proceeding to Phase 2 without resolving this creates a risk of authored schemas in a format that does not match the eventual enforcement toolchain.

The provenance section (lines 72-88) explicitly states this document is a synthesis from a ChatGPT project discussion and 'is not itself an implementation proof'. The plan is status:future and lifecycle:future with no acceptance-criteria completion evidence. However the same document asserts specific CLI command shapes (lines 432-442), frontmatter field names (lines 247-274), cardinality rules, and invariants as if ratified. These should be clearly marked as proposals pending owner ratification, not standing design decisions.

The 'blocks' relationship (line 303) is defined as 'Reverse dependency used for graph traversal and reports' — i.e. a derived inverse of 'depends_on'. If both directions are stored as explicit edges, validators must enforce bidirectional consistency. The plan does not address this invariant, which is a graph-integrity concern that should appear in the graph invariants section (lines 362-383) or be clarified as a computed virtual edge.

The plan's 'folder paths are navigation, not the complete model' principle (line 192) is architecturally sound, but the acceptance criteria (lines 556-567) do not include any test of folder-vs-frontmatter lifecycle consistency. The graph invariants section includes a folder/frontmatter contradiction check (line 383), but there is no acceptance criterion that gates completion on this being mechanically enforced rather than advisory.

The CLI surface (lines 432-442) specifies a 'linear-export --dry-run' subcommand. Phase 6 (Linear projection, line 489) is correctly sequenced after graph model stabilisation. No architectural concern; the dry-run guard is appropriate for an unratified Linear sync contract.

specialist_findings.claim: The vendor distribution assumption is load-bearing but unverified in-plan. Line 362 states the AI vendors 'are aware and have agreed to support that packaging' — this is a single-point dependency on an external commitment with no fallback path and no reference to a written agreement, timeline, or named counterpart. The plan treats this as de-risked; it is not, because vendor priorities shift and verbal alignment is not a contract.

The TPC-risk mitigation gate is named as a marketing blocker (line 369) but the plan never defines what 'sufficient mitigation' looks like, who decides it, or on what timeline. The plan treats TPC risk as a known concept (attributed to the owner's term), but the acceptance criteria for clearance are absent. If TPC mitigation stalls, marketing is indefinitely blocked with no observable exit.

The lesson-level data-availability gate (the API's missing materialised view) and the MCP-app go-to-market / school support are both explicitly listed as 'discussion — no owner yet' (line 348). These are release-readiness blockers for the MCP app stream but have no owner, no plan, and no resolution path. The assumption that they will be resolved before K3 is implicit and untested.

The strategy measures are explicitly deferred to 'Oak analytics/research experts' (lines 309-310, 268-271), with agent-invented targets prohibited. However, the plan does not record whether Oak analytics/research capacity has been confirmed, who the named contact is, or when the grounding conversation is scheduled. The assumption that Oak will provide grounded targets in time to inform the strategy corpus before the estate restructure reads the strategy is untested.

The plan assumes the no-loss audit agent is a 'dedicated primary agent running a full parallel session' (line 451) that is independent of the restructuring agent. No allocation, resourcing, or assignment mechanism for this agent is named. The assumption that a suitably independent agent will be available and correctly briefed at the moment Body 3 execution begins is implicit.

The plan assumes that idea-level trichotomy classification (good / speculative / bad) is a reliable, judgment-stable operation across ~550 documents (line 499). The approach is described as 'judgment-heavy throughout' (line 572) but no calibration mechanism, inter-agent agreement check, or owner-review gate on the classification pass is specified. The tacit assumption is that individual agent judgment at idea-granularity is consistent enough to be the input to an irreversible restructure.

The plan assumes the ICO Children's Code / target-audience decision (vision tripwire 5, lines 168-171) will come from a ruling that is externally driven, but neither names who is responsible for obtaining the ruling nor specifies the compliance lane's timeline. The assumption that this external compliance gate will resolve before K2 needs re-ratification is implicit and untracked within this plan.

The plan states the two-part vision was authored 'ahead of the settled strategy (PDR-018)' and introduces tripwires to catch upstream revision needs (lines 155-156). Vision tripwires 4 (team formation, Linear/Figma/designer arrival) and 6 (repo-as-intent-substrate thesis accepted/rejected) are not assigned a timeline or owner and have no mechanism to fire automatically. The assumption is that agents or the owner will remember to check them as conditions change.

The plan's over-structuring guard ('could it be simpler?', line 677) is a stated principle but has no external reviewer applying it. The guard is evaluated by the same agent producing the structure, which is a weak assumption about self-assessment reliability for a large, complex governance document.

The plan records the estate count as 'grown ~33% to ~550 non-archive docs' since the June 2026-06-15 survey (line 505) and explicitly treats the survey figures as stale. The assumption that the fresh survey will be practically tractable at ~550+ documents for a full idea-granular substance inventory is not stress-tested; if growth continues, the survey scope may need bounding before execution.
